 Diwali relief for 5.35 lakh Chhattisgarh staff, pensioners as govt hikes DA by 2% 
 Trending IAS Shikhar Agrawal Bengaluru Rape Delhi Rain Gandhi's Grandson Lucknow Murder Saurav Das IAS Shikhar Agrawal Bengaluru Rape Delhi Rain Gandhi's Grandson Lucknow Murder Saurav Das IAS Shikhar Agrawal Bengaluru Rape Delhi Rain Gandhi's Grandson Lucknow Murder Saurav Das Diwali relief for 5.35 lakh Chhattisgarh staff, pensioners as govt hikes DA by 2% 
 Rashmi Drolia / TNN / Oct 31, 2026, 06:51 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print मुख्यमंत्री विष्णुदेव साय ने छात्रों से संवाद किया। Raipur: In a pre-Diwali announcement, Chhattisgarh govt has increased dearness allowance (DA) for state employees and dearness relief (DR) for pensioners by two percentage points, benefiting nearly 5.35 lakh people and imposing an additional annual burden of Rs 432 crore on the state exchequer. Chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai announced on Thursday late that the revised rates would come into effect from Nov 1, 2026, raising DA and DR from the existing 58% to 60%. The decision will benefit around 3.85 lakh govt employees and 1.50 lakh pensioners across the state. The hike will cost the govt an additional Rs 36 crore per month. CM Sai said the latest hike was intended to provide financial relief ahead of Diwali. "Our govt is sensitive to the interests of employees and pensioners. This decision will provide financial relief and add to the festive joy of their families," the CM said. The increase translates into an additional 2% of basic pay for eligible employees and 2% of basic pension for pensioners. The announcement comes amid mounting pressure from employee organisations that have been demanding DA and DR at par with Central govt employees, along with payment of pending arrears. The Chhattisgarh karmachari adhikari federation, led by state convener Kamal Verma, had written to CM Sai and finance minister O P Choudhary seeking a hike before Diwali, with retrospective effect from Jan 1, 2026. On Oct 27, a federation delegation also met deputy CM Arun Sao, urging the govt to release the additional 2% DA and DR from the due date along with arrears.
